item.title: Chocolate Price Spook Families for Halloween
item.description:
BusinessWeek Radio Simulcast • Oct 30th, 2026
Chocolate Price Spook Families for Halloween
Halloween candy is getting more expensive as higher labor, energy and transportation costs continue to pressure food prices. Stew Leonard Jr., CEO of Stew Leonard’s, says bags of popular candy are up about 50 cents from last year, prompting some shoppers to trade down to cheaper options. He joins Bloomberg Businessweek Daily to discuss how affordability is changing consumer behavior, and how both environmental and economic changes are impacting the business.

item.title: Crypto Hack Reignites Regulatory Debate
item.description:
BusinessWeek Radio Simulcast • Oct 30th, 2026
Crypto Hack Reignites Regulatory Debate
A $6 billion crypto hack is putting digital-asset security back in the spotlight. Former CFTC chairman J. Christopher Giancarlo, known as “CryptoDad”, argues the attack exposed vulnerabilities at an individual firm rather than a failure of underlying blockchain technology. He is also calling for the US to take a more aggressive approach to state-sponsored cyberattacks. He joins Bloomberg Businessweek Daily to discuss the fallout from the hack and why he believes prediction markets should be regulated federally by the CFTC rather than by individual states.

item.title: PacSun CEO: Brands Mean a Lot to Young People Today
item.description:
Bloomberg The Close • Oct 30th, 2026
PacSun CEO: Brands Mean a Lot to Young People Today
Brieane Olson, CEO of PacSun, says that the retailer’s core customer is 16 to 24, while it is also tracking differences between Gen Z and Gen Alpha. Drawing on a PacSun Youth Report conducted with GlobalData and surveying 6,000 young people, Olson said mental health ranks as their top priority. She cited PACSUN’s ongoing partnership with Selena Gomez and the Rare Impact Foundation as an example of collaborations intended to have lasting value for young customers. She speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close" on October 29, 2026.

Fund 1 Investments LLC, the third-largest shareholder in Xponential Fitness Inc., the owner of Club Pilates and Pure Barre brands, said it’s pushing for a take-private and is looking to buy the company itself.
The Rincon, Puerto Rico-based investor is prepared to offer $5.61 to $7.00 per share in cash to acquire Xponential, the investor said in a filingBloomberg Terminal
Friday, confirming an earlier Bloomberg News report.

Wall Street got a reality check as a bruising selloff in technology shares fueled concern the artificial-intelligence frenzy that has powered the equity bull market might be overblown.
Disappointing tech results spurred the worst drop for stocks since June, with the Nasdaq 100 falling 3.5% and briefly crossing the threshold of a technical correction. Intel Corp. slid the most in over four decades as its outlook missed estimates. Amazon.com Inc. slipped 1.4% on greater capital spending. The S&P 500 dropped 1.8%, breaching its key 100-day moving average.
